sentences.text: Parabacteroides species are core members of the human gut microbiota, with an average abundance near 1.27 percent across twelve populations.
They metabolise carbohydrates and secrete short-chain fatty acids, and resistance to antibiotics such as clindamycin, moxifloxacin and cefoxitin has been described.
In mice, live Parabacteroides distasonis altered the bile acid profile, raising lithocholic and ursodeoxycholic acid.
Reviews report close relationships between this genus and host health, including metabolic syndrome, inflammatory bowel disease and obesity.
